## Which jar do I download?

| Jar | AUTISM Client | API |
|---|---|---|
| `bossaddon-2-pre.1.jar` | V4 / 5.1 | v4 |
| `bossaddon-2-pre.1+client5.0.jar` | 5.0 public release | v3 |

**Install only one jar.** Both require Minecraft **26.2**, Java **25+**, Fabric Loader, Fabric API **0.152.2+26.2**, and the matching AUTISM Client. Host-client dependency jars are not included.

## BossAddon v2-pre.1

This is an experimental prerelease of the BossAddon rework, published from `prerelease/v2-pre.1`. Its source has also been merged into `master`; the release remains marked as a prerelease.

### Changes

- Add 19 disabled-by-default modules: AutoMace, ten movement helpers, and eight combat/defense/ranged helpers.
- Upgrade AutoWeapon, AutoHook, AutoShoot, and InvManager.
- Remove overlapping addon modules in favor of the host client's native modules; retain AutoClutch explicitly.
- Share friend/team protection, hotbar/input ownership, and updated HUD observations across the retained module lineup.
- Support separate builds for AUTISM Client 5.0 and V4/5.1; include source attribution and license notices.

See the [versioned README](https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/blob/v2-pre.1/README.md) for the module lineup, changed behavior, and retired modules. Back up your configuration and remove the previous BossAddon jar before installing.

### Verification and limitations

- Both client-specific builds passed `build test --rerun compileGametestJava --offline --console=plain` on Java 25.
- **430 unit tests passed per build**, with zero failures, errors, or skips.
- Each build's 55 checked host-member references resolved on both local host versions.
- Both packaged jars passed metadata, entrypoint/mixin completeness, license-notice, credential-literal, and dependency/test-artifact exclusion checks. SHA-256 checksums are attached.
- Native gameplay was **not rerun for this publication**. Earlier targeted gameplay checks do not establish complete module/mode coverage; full in-world API4 QA remains unverified because of the host authentication gate. UI, performance, and clean-install gameplay are not newly verified.
- Experimental movement and timing-sensitive behavior may be corrected or rejected by servers. No anticheat compatibility is promised.

releases.notes:
## Clickable party invite and warp prompts

Both prompts that ask you a question now end with clickable answers:

```
● [BossChat] x0mx wants you to join them on divineprison.net · ?bossaddon party warp accept or decline  [Accept] [Decline]
```

Click one and it fills the exact command into your chat box; press Enter to confirm.

**Why:** a party invite and a warp request are answered by commands that differ by a single word — `?bossaddon party accept` vs `?bossaddon party **warp** accept`. Both prompts already printed the exact command, and it still didn't survive muscle memory: answering a warp with `party accept` reaches the relay's *party* path and comes back "You have no pending party invite", a message about a different feature that reads as warp being broken. 1.14.4 added a hint after the fact; this removes the retyping step that causes it.

**A deliberate choice:** the chips *suggest* the command rather than running it. The addon's commands start with `?`, not `/`, so filling the chat box keeps the line flowing through the normal interception path — which is what guarantees nothing beginning with `?` is ever sent to the server, and keeps the final Enter yours. Running it directly would bypass that and risk the command being sent as ordinary public chat. Hovering a chip shows exactly what will be filled in.

The message text still names the commands too, so typing keeps working and screenshots stay readable.

No gameplay modules changed since 1.14.1.

**Install:** drop `bossaddon-1.14.5.jar` into your mods folder (delete any older `bossaddon-*.jar` first). Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 + Fabric API for Minecraft 26.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/compare/v1.14.4...v1.14.5

releases.notes:
## Fixes a party warp dead end

A small patch. If you were sent a warp request, typed `?bossaddon party accept`, and got back **"You have no pending party invite"** — this is that.

A warp request and a party invite are answered by **different commands**, and the relay holds no warp state at all (a pending warp lives only on your own client). So answering a warp with `party accept` reaches the relay's *party* path, which correctly reports that you have no party invite — a message about a different feature, which reads as party warp being broken.

`?bossaddon party accept` and `decline` now tell you when a warp is also pending and name the command that answers it:

```
● BossChat — you also have a warp request pending · answer that one with ?bossaddon party warp accept
```

It's a hint rather than a redirect on purpose: accepting a warp moves you to another server, which is exactly the action party warp requires an explicit, unambiguous command for. Quietly treating one command as the other would undo that.

**Reminder of the two commands:**

```
?bossaddon party accept            answer a party INVITE
?bossaddon party warp accept       answer a WARP request
```

**Also:** the warp accept path now records to the game log whether a pending warp existed, its age and its TTL — that state is client-only, so it's the whole story for diagnosing any future report.

No gameplay modules changed since 1.14.1.

**Install:** drop `bossaddon-1.14.4.jar` into your mods folder (delete any older `bossaddon-*.jar` first). Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 + Fabric API for Minecraft 26.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/compare/v1.14.3...v1.14.4

releases.notes:
## Fixes BossChat identity drift and silent waits

A patch release for **BossChat**. Two faults, both of which made the feature look broken while behaving exactly as written.

### Your account could change without BossChat noticing

Relay identity was captured **once**, when the connection was made. AUTISM Client can switch accounts at runtime, and BossChat never noticed — so the relay kept calling you by the account you held when the socket opened, while the game called you the new one.

That matters because the relay routes party invites, DMs and warps **by username**. With a stale identity:
- an invite to a *different player* could resolve to your own connection, answering **"You cannot invite yourself"**;
- your old name stayed hostage, so another client trying to use it was refused with **"username is already in use"**.

BossChat now re-authenticates when the local account changes, so the name the relay knows is always the account you're actually playing.

### A sleeping relay is now announced instead of silent

The relay's host spins down after 15 minutes without HTTP traffic, so the first connection after a quiet spell pays for a wake-up. That used to be a silent exponential backoff — you saw nothing at all for up to a minute and reasonably concluded BossChat was broken.

A cold start is now told apart from a real outage at the socket level (the host's edge proxy answers the upgrade with a 5xx while it has no app running, whereas an outage produces no HTTP exchange at all), and you get:

```
● BossChat — BossRelay is starting up · estimated ~15-60s (the server sleeps when idle)…
● BossChat — still starting · 21s elapsed, check 7…
● BossChat — BossRelay is awake (24s) · connecting…
```

It polls the relay's `/health` endpoint while waiting — on this host an inbound HTTP request is what *triggers* the spin-up, so polling both detects readiness and causes it. A genuine outage says so instead, and never claims the server is starting.

### Also

- BossChat now logs **why** it fell back to unverified. `relay.offline=true` (a deliberate testing setting) and a genuinely failed Mojang handshake used to produce an identical `(unverified)` line, which is indistinguishable from a bug — if the config forced it, chat now says so and names the setting to change.
- Fixed a socket left open when a connection's handshake completed after it had already been closed.

No gameplay modules changed since 1.14.1.

**Install:** drop `bossaddon-1.14.3.jar` into your mods folder (delete any older `bossaddon-*.jar` first). Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 + Fabric API for Minecraft 26.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/compare/v1.14.2...v1.14.3

releases.notes:
## Fixes BossChat reconnects dropping party invites and warps

A patch release for **BossChat**. If you have ever been sent a party invite or a warp request, seen nothing arrive, and wondered whether the other person actually sent it — this is why.

**What was wrong:** `RelayManager.connect()` opened a new socket without closing the old one, so every reconnect left a live connection behind. The relay resolves a username to the **first** matching connection, so an account holding several sockets could have its party invites and warp requests delivered to an abandoned one. You were online, addressed correctly, and saw nothing. Reconnects are routine — the addon reconnects on any transient drop — so this accumulated over a session.

Fixing it also required `RelayClient.close()` to honour its own contract: the `closing` flag was assigned but never read, so a discarded socket kept reporting `onClose`/`onText` to the manager that had already replaced it — which would have caused a spurious extra reconnect and overwritten the new connection's state.

**Server side, already live for everyone (no update needed for these two):**
- Party invites are now keyed to your **username** instead of your connection, so an invite survives a reconnect by either side. Previously a one-second blip by *either* party silently made the invite unanswerable while the prompt stayed on your screen — that is the "it says I have no pending invite" bug.
- **Party warp now works at all.** The relay had no handler for warp frames: a warp request was silently dropped *and* counted as protocol abuse, so the tenth attempt disconnected the sender from BossChat and disbanded their party.

**Also in this release:** test coverage for the `?party warp` command tree.

No gameplay modules changed — Nuker and everything else are untouched since 1.14.1.

**Install:** drop `bossaddon-1.14.2.jar` into your mods folder (delete any older `bossaddon-*.jar` first). Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 + Fabric API for Minecraft 26.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/compare/v1.14.1...v1.14.2

releases.notes:
## Fixes Nuker (BossUtility)

The Nuker shipped in v1.14.0 **never broke non-instant blocks**. This release fixes that.

**Root cause:** every tick it acted, Nuker set `delayTimer = delay` (default 2), so the next ticks returned early. But legit mining needs an uninterrupted `continueDestroyBlock` stream on a single block — progress decays the moment it stops — so any block that wasn't instant-breakable reset to zero forever. The per-tick loop also burst-started `maxPerTick` blocks, each one cancelling the previous.

**What changed**
- Legit mining now runs continuously on **one block until it breaks**, and only then applies the between-block delay. The `maxPerTick` burst and the delay gate now apply only to the instant paths (packet mine / interact), which complete in a single action.
- Line-of-sight raycast uses the block **outline** instead of the collider, so no-collision blocks (grass, flowers) are targetable at the default `wallsRange` of 0.
- New **Debug messages** toggle — chats a once-a-second filter breakdown (scanned / air / unbreakable / mode / list / tool / sight skips + target count) so you can see exactly why nothing is being targeted.
- An empty whitelist now **warns once on enable** instead of silently doing nothing.

**Reminder:** Nuker still ships safe by default — list mode is Whitelist with an empty list, so it breaks nothing until you add blocks.

> ⚠️ Nuker is the most destructive module in the addon. The instant-mine / no-cooldown / interact options are the most anticheat-detectable — leave them off on servers with anticheat.

**Install:** drop `bossaddon-1.14.1.jar` into your mods folder (delete any older `bossaddon-*.jar` first). Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 + Fabric API for Minecraft 26.2.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/WaterBoss11/BossAddon/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1

releases.notes:
BossAddon v1.12.1 is a patch release: one real bug fix plus one new UI feature. No settings reset - your config and module setup carry over.

## Fixed: the utility half toggle now acts on real modules
`?bossaddon utility on|off` reported success but did nothing - it always found zero utility modules, so turning the utility half off or on never actually changed anything (while the pvp half worked correctly). BossAddon now figures out which modules belong to each half from AUTISM's live module list, matched by name-space ("boss-pvp:" vs "boss-utility:") - the same modules AUTISM's own menu shows - instead of relying on a list that could come up empty. The utility half now correctly disables and restores its own modules, matching how the pvp half already behaved.

## New: a visual suggestion popup for "?" commands
Typing a "?" command now shows a small popup above the chat input listing the matching completions - subcommands and their arguments - the same visual role as the vanilla "/" command dropdown (which is hardcoded to "/" and cannot be reused for "?"). The list updates live as you type and highlights the entry Tab would select next. Pressing Tab still does the actual insertion and cycles through the options as before; the popup is purely a visual guide to what the options are.

## Install
- Download `bossaddon-1.12.1.jar` and drop it in your mods folder, removing any older `bossaddon-*.jar`.
- This single jar contains both halves (PVP and utility). If you still have a separate `boss-pvp` or `boss-utility` jar from before the merge, remove it - keeping it alongside this jar would double-load and crash Fabric.
- Requires AUTISM Client 3.4 on Minecraft 26.2.

The in-game update checker will flag any 1.12.0 or older install as outdated against 1.12.1.

releases.notes:
## ⚠️ IMPORTANT — delete your old jar first

This release **renames the jar file** (and the mod's displayed id) from `boss-pvp` to `bossaddon`. Because the filename changed, dropping in the new jar does **not** overwrite the old one.

**You MUST manually delete your old `boss-pvp-*.jar` from your mods folder before adding the new `bossaddon-1.11.1.jar`, or Minecraft will fail to load due to a duplicate mod ID error.**

**Your settings are fully preserved — only the file name and the displayed mod name have changed.** Module tuning, which modules are enabled, menu mode, and all other config carry over untouched.

### How to update
1. **Delete** `boss-pvp-*.jar` from your `mods/` folder.
2. Add **`bossaddon-1.11.1.jar`**.
3. Launch as normal — everything is exactly where you left it.

---

## What changed
An **identity/packaging patch — no new functionality**:

- Jar filename: `boss-pvp-<version>.jar` → **`bossaddon-<version>.jar`**
- Fabric mod id: `boss-pvp` → **`bossaddon`** (it still `provides` `boss-pvp` for compatibility)
- The mod already displayed as "BossAddon"; now the id and file name match it.

Internally the per-module settings namespace and config file deliberately stay `boss-pvp` — that is exactly **why nothing resets** on this update.

Everything from **v1.11.0** is unchanged here: the `?bossaddon` command system, public-facing BossChat with party + party-warp, and the Velocity Crash Guard / AntiEntityPush Modify mode / reconfigure-loop guard.

## Boss's PVP v1.10.1

A menu usability + housekeeping update. No combat behavior changed — this is all about making the menu easier to read and use, plus one behavior change to the update checker (called out below).

### Simpler, cleaner module menu
- **Every module and setting description was shortened** to a short, plain-language line, so you can tell what something does at a glance instead of reading a paragraph.
- **New Simple / Advanced menu mode.** By default the menu now shows only each module's handful of everyday settings (the main toggles and the couple of values most people actually change). The technical tuning knobs are hidden until you ask for them. Switch modes with a command:
  - `/bosspvp menu advanced` — show every setting
  - `/bosspvp menu simple` — back to the essentials (this is the default)
  - `/bosspvp menu` — toggle between the two

  Your settings are never lost — Advanced just reveals the extra ones; anything you'd already set keeps working either way.
- **New "Client" category.** The two non-combat utility toggles — **Crash & Kick Reports** and **Update Checker** — now live in their own **Client** category, out of the way of the PvP modules.

### The update checker is now always on
The launch-time update check (which tells you in chat + on the HUD when a newer version is out) **no longer has an off switch — it now always runs on launch.** Being upfront about this: the previous opt-out setting has been removed.

It stays exactly as limited as before: it is **read-only** and sends **no personal information**. The only thing that leaves your client is a single plain request to GitHub's public releases API for this repo — the same request your browser makes when you open the releases page. Nothing is ever downloaded or installed, and if GitHub is unreachable the check simply does nothing. (Crash & Kick reporting is unaffected and stays **fully optional** — you can still turn that off.)

---
**Install:** drop `boss-pvp-1.10.1.jar` into your `mods` folder (replacing any older `boss-pvp` jar) alongside AUTISM Client for Minecraft 26.2.

## Boss's PVP v1.9.1

### New: launch-time update checker
On launch, the addon now makes a single **read-only** request to the GitHub Releases API and, if your installed build is behind the latest release, tells you — with a one-time chat notice (including a link to the release page) and a small, passive HUD indicator. It's fire-and-forget: if GitHub is unreachable or the check fails for any reason, it fails silently and never blocks startup.

- **Read-only by design** — nothing is ever downloaded, extracted, or installed. It only reads the latest release tag and notifies you.
- **No telemetry** — no data leaves your client beyond the plain API request itself (the same request a browser makes when opening the releases page).
- **Opt out anytime** — toggle off the **"Update Checker"** module and no GitHub request is made at all.

### Fixed: version reporting (the reason this release exists)
Previous builds baked their internal version as `1.0.0` even as release tags advanced — so the new update checker would have compared `1.0.0` against the latest tag and reported a **permanent false "outdated"** notice for everyone. This release fixes the convention: the baked version now tracks the release tag (this build reports **1.9.1**, and the jar is named `boss-pvp-1.9.1.jar`). Going forward, the internal version and the git tag move together on every release.

### Also included
- **AutoWeapon charge gate:** KillAura's full-charge gate now evaluates against the weapon AutoWeapon will actually swing on the attack tick, not the currently held item — so a sword→axe swap no longer slips an under-charged hit through.

---
**Install:** drop `boss-pvp-1.9.1.jar` into your `mods` folder (replacing any older `boss-pvp` jar) alongside AUTISM Client for Minecraft 26.2.
